common_name: Pretoria Canna (Bengal Tiger Canna, Striped Yellow-Green Foliage Canna)

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring and plant in rich, moist, well-drained soil when soil temperatures are above 60°F; each division should have at least one eye. In zone 9, established clumps overwinter in the ground and resprout vigorously each spring.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun, and feed with a balanced fertilizer monthly during the growing season for the best foliage color and flowering. Pretoria, also widely sold as Bengal Tiger, bears large, paddle-shaped leaves boldly striped in yellow-green and dark green, topped by bright orange flowers held well above the foliage on tall stalks, creating strong tropical impact as a specimen or mass planting. It grows taller than many striped-leaf canna cultivars, adding presence to the back of a border or a large container planting. Foliage color and striping are most vivid in full sun, fading toward plain green in shade. In zone 9 it overwinters reliably in the ground; provide consistent moisture, since cannas are heavy feeders and drinkers, but ensure good drainage, since standing water causes rhizome rot.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Canna Growing Guide

common_name: Australia Canna (Glossy Near-Black Foliage Red-Flowered Canna)

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring and plant in rich, moist, well-drained soil when soil temperatures are above 60°F; Australia is grown as much for its near-black glossy foliage as for its flowers.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun. Australia bears large, glossy, deep burgundy-black leaves that hold their dark color through the growing season, one of the darkest and glossiest canna foliage colors available, topped by clear red flowers that stand out sharply against the near-black backdrop. It works well as a bold foliage accent in a tropical-style border or large container, either alone or paired with chartreuse or silver companions for maximum contrast. Feed monthly during the growing season for the best color and bloom, and keep soil consistently moist but well-drained, since cannas are heavy feeders and drinkers but suffer rhizome rot in standing water. In zone 9 it overwinters reliably in the ground, resprouting vigorously each spring.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Canna Growing Guide
Louisiana State University AgCenter — Tropical Plants for Gulf South Gardens

common_name: Wyoming Canna (Classic Bronze-Purple Foliage Orange-Flowered Canna)

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring and plant in rich, moist, well-drained soil when soil temperatures are above 60°F; Wyoming is a classic, long-cultivated bronze-leaved canna still widely grown for its reliable performance.

directions: Plant rhizomes 3-4 inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun. Wyoming is a classic, long-cultivated canna bearing large bronze-purple leaves and vivid orange flowers held on tall stalks well above the foliage, a reliable, vigorous performer that has remained popular for generations despite the arrival of many newer striped and dark-leaved canna cultivars. Its tall stature makes it well suited to the back of a border, a poolside planting, or a large container where its tropical presence can be fully appreciated. Feed monthly during the growing season for the best foliage color and flowering, and keep soil consistently moist but well-drained, since standing water causes rhizome rot. In zone 9 it overwinters reliably in the ground, expanding by rhizome division each year.
